Information Hierarchy: Live floor first; waiting parties at left; server roster and cover counts in context
Spatial Grammar: Dining areas contain positioned tables with capacity; drag or select a party to seat; assigned-server color and turn-time border stay on the table
State Vocabulary: Available; Seated; Ordered; Paid; Dirty; Blocked
Conflict Behavior: Overlapping reservations turn red; unavailable servers require an explicit swap before seating
Accessibility Alternative: Sortable table list with table, capacity, status, server, elapsed turn time, and compatible waiting parties
DPF Rationale: Adopt the live state and one-action seating grammar; adapt away from color-only status and long-press-only interaction

Information Hierarchy: Floor plan and waitlist are the shift command surface; shift overview and turn-time reporting remain secondary
Spatial Grammar: Custom floor plan with flexible table inventory, table types, server sections, and recommended assignments
State Vocabulary: Available inventory; assigned; seated; POS-derived table status; waiting; notified
Conflict Behavior: Recommendations expose compatible tables while inventory and pacing controls prevent overbooking
Accessibility Alternative: List of tables and parties with capacity, area, server section, status, quote, and recommendation reason
DPF Rationale: Adopt fast host-stand hierarchy and assignment recommendations; preserve operator confirmation and explain constraints

Information Hierarchy: Day calendar first; team members and resources form lanes; waitlist and gaps stay adjacent
Spatial Grammar: Time grid crosses staff and bookable resources such as chairs or rooms; appointments reserve service duration and buffers
State Vocabulary: Available; booked; blocked time; waiting; notified; in service; complete
Conflict Behavior: Staff skill, availability, resource, duration, and group alignment prevent overlap and double-booking
Accessibility Alternative: Agenda table grouped by provider with time, client, service, resource, status, gap, and conflict reason
DPF Rationale: Adopt provider-resource joint availability and intelligent gap filling; make chairs explicit resources and never rely on calendar position alone

Information Hierarchy: Date occupancy summary first; room rows and reservation bars below; unassigned accommodations and inspection needs are prominent
Spatial Grammar: Rooms form rows across a date grid; reservation bars span stays; drag-and-drop assigns or moves rooms; locks and blocks constrain movement
State Vocabulary: In-House; Confirmed; Confirmation Pending; Checked Out; Out of Service; Courtesy Hold; Blocked; Needs Inspection; Locked Assignment
Conflict Behavior: Unassigned count opens assignment; locked rooms resist auto-assignment; overlaps, blocks, room type, and inspection state constrain placement
Accessibility Alternative: Room assignment table by date with room, guest/reservation, arrival, departure, state, block, inspection, and assignment lock
DPF Rationale: Adopt occupancy grid and explicit unassigned demand; simplify the state palette and pair every icon/color with text

Information Hierarchy: Availability and location first; upcoming pickup/return fulfillment next; maintenance and performance remain visible
Spatial Grammar: Trackable units or bulk stock are grouped by product and location with a date-range availability horizon; barcode handoff changes custody
State Vocabulary: Available; reserved; picked; rented out; awaiting return; returned; downtime; maintenance
Conflict Behavior: Real-time availability prevents overbooking; buffers and downtime block unsafe adjacency; multi-location stock is separate
Accessibility Alternative: Inventory table with unit or quantity, product, location, availability range, custody state, next pickup/return, downtime, and conflict
DPF Rationale: Adopt unit identity, location, date-range availability, buffers, and downtime; add a spatial yard lens only where a business maintains meaningful bays

Information Hierarchy: Portfolio and association context first; maintenance and architectural requests flow into tracked work with board visibility
Spatial Grammar: Community and property locations anchor requests; work orders connect location, resident or common area, vendor, approvals, notes, and evidence
State Vocabulary: Submitted; triaged; assigned; scheduled; in progress; awaiting approval; complete; closed
Conflict Behavior: Priority, due date, board/vendor approval, access, budget, and duplicate-location work constrain action
Accessibility Alternative: Priority work table grouped by association/property with location, request, impact, due date, owner, vendor, approval, status, and next action
DPF Rationale: Adopt the property-linked system of record and mobile field evidence; elevate current priorities and blocked next actions above generic portfolio maps

Information Hierarchy: My action items and open work lead; association or property context and configured workflow stage remain visible
Spatial Grammar: Work orders attach to an association or exact property/GPS location and progress through configurable action-item steps
State Vocabulary: Open; closed; configured workflow step; follow-up due; completion due
Conflict Behavior: Role ownership, due/follow-up dates, board action, service provider, and immutable property association govern progression
Accessibility Alternative: Action-item table with association/property, GPS/location text, service type, follower, provider, workflow step, follow-up, due date, and status
DPF Rationale: Adopt role-owned workflow and location precision; normalize configured states into a stable DPF priority vocabulary while preserving source labels

Information Hierarchy: Unassigned daily and weekly job trays remain beside technician schedule; alerts and route context surface exceptions
Spatial Grammar: Technicians form schedule lanes while a map supplies current location and route; jobs move from queue to compatible technician windows
State Vocabulary: Unassigned; scheduled; dispatched; traveling; working; paused; complete; canceled; alert
Conflict Behavior: Skill, business unit, availability, current job cycle, arrival window, traffic, capacity, overlaps, and route efficiency constrain assignment
Accessibility Alternative: Dispatch table grouped by technician with job order, window, location, travel estimate, skill fit, state, alert, conflict, and queued demand
DPF Rationale: Adopt queue-plus-schedule-plus-map grammar and visible job-cycle state; keep optimization advisory, explain tradeoffs, and require confirmation for conflict-causing moves
